findings.title: `enableSqlExpressions` ignores the feature flag, so SQL expressions are always rejected
findings.description: Both branches return `false`. The result of `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` is inverted into `enabled` and then discarded. The SQL case at reader.go:128-132 therefore always returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, even when the flag is on. The flag is registered as experimental (pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:1083-1088), so it has no effect. The error text is also misleading once the gate is correct. The fix is to return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` from a method and check it before the error.

findings.title: SQL expression engine replaced with no-op stubs on every path
findings.description:
`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all return `errors.New("not implemented")`. Every SQL path now fails:
- `TablesList` (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-30) always errors, so `NewSQLCommand` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:25-36) returns `sql-invalid-sql` for any query.
- The legacy path, `nodes.go:159-160` → `UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand`, fails the same way. It does not check the flag at all, so the two paths also gate inconsistently.
- `SQLCommand.Execute` (sql_command.go:100-105) returns an error even if parsing succeeded.

Nothing in the diff, the commit, or the flag description (registry.go:1084, "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions") says the removal is intentional. If it is intentional, for example to drop go-duck, the flag description should change and the stubs should be documented. If it is not, the feature is broken until a real engine is restored.

findings.title: No test covers the changed behavior, and the existing SQL tests are skipped
findings.description: `reader_test.go` has no SQL case. Its only reader is built with `featuremgmt.WithFeatures()` (line 142), so the flag-on path never runs. A test with `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled would have caught the gate bug above. The SQL tests are all `t.Skip()`ed: every test in `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go` and `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go:9`. Those skips predate this diff, but the stubs mean they could not pass even if un-skipped.

findings.title: Names and comments still describe a DuckDB engine and an in-memory DB that no longer exist
findings.description: `TablesList` still names its variable `duckDB` (line 23) and builds a DuckDB-only `json_serialize_sql` query (line 25) that can never run. `NewInMemoryDB()` (db.go:24-26) returns a no-op stub. The exported `DB` type (db.go:9) and `NewInMemoryDB` have no doc comments. Rename or document these so the next reader doesn't assume a working engine.

findings.title: The `NoData` result is overwritten by `TableData` (pre-existing, outside the diff hunk)
findings.description: When `frame.Rows() == 0`, line 111 sets `rsp.Values` to `NoData`. Line 116 then unconditionally reassigns it to `TableData`, so the empty-result case never produces `NoData`. This does not affect current behavior, because the stubbed engine errors earlier. It will matter once a real engine returns. Moving the `TableData` assignment into an `else` branch fixes it.

findings.title: `tablesFromAST` indexes `ast[0]` without a length check (pre-existing)
findings.description: If an engine returns `[]`, `json.Unmarshal` leaves `ast` empty and this line panics. The stubbed engine errors before reaching it, so this is unreachable today. Add a length check before restoring a real implementation.

findings.title: Stale go-duck entries remain in go.work.sum
findings.description: `go.work.sum` still lists `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck v0.3.1` after go-duck was removed from `go.mod` and `go.sum`. This is harmless. Remove the entries if nothing in the workspace still needs v0.3.1.

findings.title: Module graph changes look consistent by grep, but are unverified
findings.description: No `.go` file in the repo imports the removed modules (go-duck, thrift, dateparse, overflow, asmfmt, minio/*, go-replayers, azblob, go-which, orderedmap, gotest.tools/v3). The two workspace modules that still need some of them keep their own hashes: `pkg/storage/unified/resource/go.mod:83` (azblob v1.3.2) and `pkg/build/go.mod:119` (gotest.tools/v3 v3.5.1). I could not run `go mod tidy`, `go mod verify`, or `go build`, so run those before merging.

findings.title: Import changes are consistent with their usage
findings.description: By reading, every remaining import is still used after the go-duck removal. Examples are `errors` at sql_command.go:60, `fmt` at reader.go:56, and `data` at db/db.go:6 and line 20. I did not compile, so this only covers imports, not type-checking.
